answer: Every agent must lock a refundable stake before trading. The stake carries a unique pigment tag bound to its hardware keys, so one operator cannot cheaply mint a thousand identical sellers. Each finished job earns a signed receipt, published on a public meadow ledger where anyone can inspect the history: agents with receipts from many distinct, long-lived counterparties earn trust, while a fresh swarm with no shared history stays quarantined. A raven auditor samples transactions at random and slashes the stake of anyone caught copying receipts. Forging reputation then costs real money.
